purpose: Teach: しっぽ/のび/安らぎ/染まっ/くっきり/出先/とろ/割る

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、飼ってた犬、絶対、しっぽ、絶対、よく、振ってくれたわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, that dog of yours really did wag its tail all the time, didn't it? You remember, don't you?
lines.style: Soft, distant gaze into memory. Warm nostalgia. Slight pause before names. Voice trails upward gently on the question, checking she's still with him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、二人で、絶対、のびのびと、絶対、過ごしたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes. When we were young, the two of us spent such carefree days together. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Quiet affirmation. Gentle emphasis on 'together.' Voice holds steady and warm, like settling into a familiar chair. The question is tender, not urgent.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 庭で、本気で、絶対、お茶を飲む、絶対、安らぎの時間、絶対、本当に、絶対、大切ね、ばあさん
lines.en: Those afternoons in the garden, having tea together—that quiet time really was precious, wasn't it?
lines.style: Measured, almost meditative pace. Soft landing on 'precious.' Each phrase given weight without rush. Voice carries the weight of understanding what time has taken from those days.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔、本気で、絶対、桜、絶対、ピンクに、絶対、染まった、絶対、思い出、絶対、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Long ago, I remember the cherry blossoms turning everything pink. That memory stays with me still.
lines.style: Eyes half-closed. Voice drifts into the image itself. Slower tempo on color and memory. Gentle, almost singing quality at the edges. Trails softly at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃の写真、本気で、絶対、くっきり、絶対、写ってるわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: The photographs from back then—they really did capture it all so clearly. Do you remember looking at them together?
lines.style: Slightly stronger, more present. Pride in the sharpness of the memory. Voice brightens just a touch on 'clearly,' then softens into the question—inviting her back into the shared moment.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 息子、本気で、絶対、お出先から、絶対、心配して、絶対、電話、絶対、くれたわよ、あなた
lines.en: Our son would call from wherever he was, always checking in on us. He still does that, doesn't he?
lines.style: Voice steadies with gentle pride. Warmth on mentioning the son's care. Slight catch or warmth on the realization of continuity. Quiet gratitude underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔、本気で、絶対、とろっとした、絶対、お祖母ちゃんの煮物、絶対、美味しかったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Your grandmother's stewed dishes were so tender and delicious. I still think about those meals sometimes.
lines.style: Wistful appetite in the voice. Slight savoring quality, like tasting memory. Warm, almost childlike appreciation. Voice softens at the end, holding the comfort of it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 最近、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、お皿、絶対、割ること、絶対、増えてきたわよね、あなた、本気で、絶対、お互いに、注意しましょうね、絶対、本気、本気で、絶対。
lines.en: Lately, you know, I've been breaking dishes more often. We need to watch out for each other now, don't we? We really do.
lines.style: Gentle shift to present moment. Careful, loving concern. Not anxious—factual but wrapped in affection. Slight hesitation before repeating 'really'—acknowledging both of their fragility with quiet dignity.
